item.title: Conjugator length of Bestvina-Brady groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.05619v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify the conjugator length functions of Bestvina-Brady groups. We show that the conjugator length function, when non-trivial, grows as a linear or quadratic polynomial. In fact, we give explicit criteria on the defining graph to determine the precise degree of the polynomial. The proof generalises ideas of Bridson, Riley, and Sale by exploiting the framework developed by Chang and the authors to classify the Dehn functions of Bestvina-Brady groups.
item.dc:creator: Jer\'onimo Garc\'ia-Mej\'ia, Matteo Migliorini

item.title: Assouad--Nagata dimension of systolic complexes with almost flat intervals
item.description: arXiv:2611.05763v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce the notion of systolic complexes with almost flat intervals. They constitute a subclass of fit systolic complexes and arise naturally in the study of graphical C(3)--T(6) small cancellation complexes. We prove that their Assouad--Nagata dimension is bounded above by a universal constant. As consequences, we obtain universal bounds on the Assouad--Nagata dimension of tame simply connected graphical C(3)--T(6) small cancellation complexes and of finitely generated groups defined by graphical C(3)--T(6) small cancellation presentations. In the appendix, we observe that the proof of finiteness of asymptotic dimension for buildings due to Dymara and Schick also yields finiteness of their asymptotic Assouad--Nagata dimension.
item.dc:creator: Mart\'in Blufstein, Victor Chepoi, Huaitao Gui, Damian Osajda

item.title: Large orbits of $p$-groups on conjugacy classes
item.description: arXiv:2611.05904v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $P$ be a $p$-group that acts faithfully and coprimely on a finite group $H$. A classical result of D.\ S.\ Passman, in the form proved by I.\ M.\ Isaacs, asserts that there exists an element $x\in H$ such that $|C_P(x)|\le (|P|/p)^{1/p}$. In this paper, we study the corresponding question for the action of $P$ on the conjugacy classes of $H$. We show that for every odd prime $p$ the analogue of Isaacs' bound fails for classes. On the other hand, we prove that if $H$ is solvable, then there always exists a conjugacy class $c$ of $H$ whose stabilizer in $P$ has order at most $|P|^{1/2}$, and that this bound is best possible for every prime $p$. As a consequence, there always exists an irreducible character of $H$ whose inertia group in $P$ has order at most $|P|^{1/2}$. The proof proceeds via a result on linear actions of $p$-nilpotent groups, and in the quasiprimitive case it relies on a classification of Holt and Yang and on computer calculations.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Michael Keller

item.title: Galois's lost proof on $PSL(2,p)$
item.description: arXiv:2611.06054v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In his famous ``testamentary letter'' Galois formulated several results without proof. Among them he claimed --- here we express it in modern terms --- that the projective special linear group $PSL(2,p)$ has a subgroup of index $p$ only for $p\le 11$. Nowadays this result is seen as a corollary of the complete enumeration of all subgroups of $PSL(2,p)$ obtained by Gierster in 1881. In this paper we attempt to give a proof that uses only methods available to Galois.
item.dc:creator: P\'eter P. P\'alfy

item.title: Lifts of Brauer characters and vertex pairs for odd primes
item.description: arXiv:2611.06903v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $p$ be an odd prime, let $G$ be a finite $p$-solvable group, and let $\varphi\in\IBr_p(G)$ have vertex $Q$. We prove that $\varphi$ has at most $|Q:Q'|$ lifts to ordinary irreducible characters, establishing Cossey's conjecture for odd primes.
item.dc:creator: Yong Yang

item.title: Non-Pseudo-Arithmetic Hyperbolic 4-Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.05795v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give three explicit finite-volume hyperbolic Coxeter lattices in dimension four whose adjoint trace fields are not totally real. They are the reflection groups of the Ma--Zheng polytopes $P_{11,6}$, $P_{11,7}$, $P_{11,8}$. The obstruction is contained in two cyclic products of the doubled unit-normal Gram matrix $A=2G$. Those products recover elements $s=\sqrt5$ and $u$ satisfying $$ (s-1)u^2+2(s-3)u+s-7=0. $$ After the embedding $s\mapsto-\sqrt5$, this quadratic has discriminant $8(1-\sqrt5)<0$. The cyclic-product field therefore has a complex place. Vinberg's identification of that field with the adjoint trace field and the Emery--Mila total-reality obstruction imply that the three lattices are not pseudo-arithmetic. Torsion-free orientation-preserving finite-index subgroups yield orientable noncompact finite-volume hyperbolic $4$-manifolds with the same obstruction. Exact computations check the census data and provide independent field and finite-volume certificates. A pinned Lean~4 development verifies the radical identity and the number-field obstruction. It also checks the lattice and manifold implications conditional on explicit geometric and literature hypotheses.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Kolpakov

item.title: On the Cameron-Praeger conjecture for Steiner 6-designs
item.description: arXiv:2611.06081v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A long-standing and far-reaching conjecture of Cameron and Praeger (1993) asserts that no non-trivial block-transitive $6$-$(v,k,\lambda)$ designs exist. Huber (2010) reduced the Steiner case ($\lambda=1$) to a single infinite family of possible exceptions, where the automorphism group is $G=\PGaL(2,p^e)$ acting on the points of the projective line, with $p\in\{2,3\}$ and $e$ an odd prime power. In this paper, we resolve this final case. By combining orbit-stabiliser analysis for the action of specific involutions in $\PGaL(2,p^e)$ with the modular arithmetic constraints derived from the design parameters, we prove that no such Steiner 6-designs can exist for any admissible $q$. This completes the proof that the Cameron-Praeger conjecture is true for the important case of non-trivial Steiner 6-designs.
item.dc:creator: Ximin Wang, Zheng Huang, Weijun Liu

item.title: A characterization of a family of integral Cayley graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.06581v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $G$ be a finite group and $H$ be a subgroup of $G$. In our earlier work, we proved that the quasi-strongly regular Cayley graph $\Gamma_H(G)$ is integral whenever $H$ is normal in $G$, and raised the question of whether the converse also holds. In this paper, we answer this question affirmatively. We prove that if $\Gamma_H(G)$ is integral, then $H$ must be a normal subgroup of $G$. Consequently, $\Gamma_H(G)$ is integral if and only if $H\lhd G$. Our proof uses the irreducible representations of $G$ and the dimensions of their $H$-fixed subspaces. For a non-normal subgroup $H$, we construct a two-dimensional invariant subspace of a suitable representation operator and show that the corresponding eigenvalues are irrational.
item.dc:creator: Sauvik Poddar, Sucharita Biswas

item.title: Boxicity of Power Graphs of Finite Nilpotent Groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.06816v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The \textit{boxicity} of an undirected graph $\Gamma$, denoted as $\operatorname{box}(\Gamma)$, is the smallest non-negative integer $d$ such that $\Gamma$ can be represented as the intersection graph of axis-parallel rectangular boxes in $\mathbb{R}^d$. The \emph{power graph} of a group $G$, denoted as $\operatorname{Pow}(G)$, is an undirected graph whose vertex set is the group itself, with two elements being adjacent if one is a power of the other. We determine the exact boxicity of power graphs of finite nilpotent groups. For a cyclic group of order $n=\prod_{i=1}^{r}p_i^{e_i}>1$, where the $p_i$ are distinct primes, we prove that its power graph has boxicity $\sum_{i=1}^{r}e_i-\max_i e_i$. For a finite nilpotent group $G$, let the number of noncyclic odd Sylow subgroups be denoted by $t(G)$. If $G$ has odd order or if $G$ has a cyclic Sylow $2$-subgroup, then $\operatorname{box}(\operatorname{Pow}(G))=\operatorname{box}(\operatorname{Pow}(\mathbb{Z}_{\operatorname{exp}(G)}))+t(G)$, where $\operatorname{exp}(G)$ denotes the \emph{exponent} of a group $G$. When the Sylow $2$-subgroup is noncyclic, and the odd part is nontrivial, the boxicity equals this value or one more, and we characterise precisely when each of these values is attained. The boxicity of power graphs of arbitrary finite groups and the exact boxicity of the comparability graph of the Boolean lattice were posed as open questions in Discrete Mathematics, 349(7):115017, 2026. As a consequence of our results, we answer the latter question completely and the former question partially, by computing the exact boxicity of the power graphs of nilpotent groups.
item.dc:creator: L. Sunil Chandran, Jinia Ghosh, Suraj Kumar Sahoo

item.title: The full Kolakoski shift is topologically transitive
item.description: arXiv:2611.06878v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that the full Kolakoski shift---namely, the subshift of all smooth sequences over the alphabet $\{1,2\}$---is topologically transitive. Consequently, we demonstrate the existence of a smooth sequence whose factors are invariant under both reversal and bitwise complementation. As a further application, we prove the existence of arbitrarily long smooth words containing an equal number of occurrences of the symbols $1$ and $2$, providing evidence in support of Keane's conjecture. Our approach leverages the hierarchical structure of the full Kolakoski shift to reimagine the shift action in terms of a self-similar semigroup, which allows techniques from group theory and combinatorics to be applied.
item.dc:creator: Andrew C. Mitchell, James J. Walton, Michael F. Whittaker

item.title: Strongly Regular Graphs of Rank Four
item.description: arXiv:2510.25410v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Strongly regular graphs are regular graphs with a constant number of common neighbours between adjacent vertices, and a constant number of common neighbours between non-adjacent vertices. These graphs have been of great interest over the last few decades and often give rise to interesting groups of automorphisms. In this paper we take a reverse approach, and leverage strong classification results on rank four permutation groups to classify the strongly regular graphs which yield such groups as a group of automorphisms.
item.dc:creator: William H. Allen

item.title: Every finite group admits a just finite presentation
item.description: arXiv:2605.10402v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A finite presentation < X | R > of a finite group is called `just finite' if removing any relation from R results in a presentation for an infinite group. It has been an open question (Kourovka Notebook, Problem 21.10) whether every finite group admits such a presentation. We resolve this conjecture in the affirmative.
item.dc:creator: Marc Lackenby

item.title: Combining Determinism and Indeterminism
item.description: arXiv:2009.03996v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Our goal is to construct mathematical operations that combine indeterminism measured from quantum randomness with computational determinism so that non-mechanistic behavior is preserved in the computation. Formally, some results about operations applied to computably enumerable (c.e.) and bi-immune sets are proven here, where the objective is for the operations to preserve bi-immunity. While developing rearrangement operations on the natural numbers, we discovered that the bi-immune rearrangements generate an uncountable subgroup of the infinite symmetric group (Sym$(\mathbb{N})$) on the natural numbers $\mathbb{N}$. This new uncountable subgroup is called the bi-immune symmetric group. We show that the bi-immune symmetric group contains the finitary symmetric group on the natural numbers, and consequently is highly transitive. Furthermore, the bi-immune symmetric group is dense in Sym$(\mathbb{N})$ with respect to the pointwise convergence topology. The complete structure of the bi-immune symmetric group and its subgroups generated by one or more bi-immune rearrangements is unknown.
item.dc:creator: Michael Stephen Fiske

item.title: Product sets in sets of returns and positivity of symmetric ergodic averages
item.description: arXiv:2608.02873v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study sets of (measurable) returns in countable groups $G$, namely sets of the form $\{g\in G:\mu(A\cap T_gA)>0\}$ arising from measure-preserving actions. Extending a result of Bergelson, we show that sets of returns in $G\times G$ contain subsets of the form $B\times B$, where $B$ is large with respect to suitable notions of largeness that remain meaningful even for non-amenable groups. As a consequence, if $G$ is amenable, then every sufficiently large subset $A\subseteq G\times G$ satisfies $B\times B\subseteq AA^{-1}$ for some large set $B\subseteq G$. We also investigate when sets of returns in $G$ contain product sets $BB$ with $B$ large. In contrast with the Cartesian-product phenomenon above, this problem is considerably subtler in non-abelian groups and is closely connected to `symmetric correlation functions', namely functions of the form $g\mapsto \mu(T_g^{-1}A\cap T_gA)$. We use this connection to show that, for broad classes of amenable groups - including finitely generated nilpotent groups and certain solvable non-nilpotent groups, every sufficiently large set $A\subseteq G$ contains a large subset $B$ satisfying $BB\subseteq AA^{-1}$. Finally, we establish polynomial analogues of these results for finitely generated nilpotent groups, extending earlier work of Bergelson and Ruzsa.
item.dc:creator: Vitaly Bergelson, Sa\'ul Rodr\'iguez-Mart\'in

item.title: Singular Loci of SL2(C)-Representation Varieties of Torus Knot Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.32064v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $T(q,p)=\langle x,y\mid x^p=y^q\rangle$, where $p,q>1$ are relatively prime, and let \[ R=\Hom(T(q,p),\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb C)). \] We compute the integral homology of the singular locus of $R$. We show that this locus has complex dimension $2$ and is a disjoint union of $\mu=(p-1)(q-1)$ smooth affine surfaces, each homotopy equivalent to the two-dimensional sphere. Consequently, \[ H_0(\Sing R;\Z)\cong H_2(\Sing R;\Z)\cong\Z^\mu, \] and all remaining homology groups vanish. Thus both nonzero Betti numbers equal the first Betti number of the Milnor fiber of the plane curve singularity $z^p+w^q=0$, namely its Milnor number $\mu$.
item.dc:creator: S. Liriano
